claims.text: Monte Carlo-based phase-field simulations coupled with ab initio data will enable precise control of phase evolution in as-cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
An as-cast or thermally unoptimized Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA contains multiple constituent phases.
Mapping the free-energy landscape can predict optimum annealing temperatures for Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Mapping the free-energy landscape can predict optimum cooling rates for Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Phase evolution is governed by the balance between nucleation and growth of ordered and disordered phases.
Local phase-boundary configurations mediate the balance between phase nucleation and growth.
Mapping a free-energy landscape reveals kinetic barriers and thermodynamic driving forces for phase transformations.
Knowledge of transformation barriers and driving forces permits processing conditions to be tuned to enhance nucleation of desired phases.
Knowledge of transformation barriers and driving forces permits processing conditions to suppress unwanted phase transitions.
Computationally guided thermal processing will produce a refined microstructure with a controlled phase mixture, distribution, and stability.
The controlled microstructure will improve mechanical or functional properties relative to conventional thermal treatments.
Empirical thermal treatments without computational guidance provide less control over phase evolution.
The effectiveness of computationally guided phase control is constrained by the accuracy of the underlying free-energy models.
The method may be limited to typical processing-temperature and processing-time regimes for Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Phase stability and resulting improvements may vary with changes in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni composition.
